7334c5b0a253f0211e1a8c9f76666c0c4fdf75db: This in-silico analysis of CCND1 (Cyclin D1) SNPs identifies four missense variants potentially destabilising the protein and links high CCND1 expression to reduced breast-cancer survival. Relevance to this thesis is partial: it engages with breast-cancer biology and variant-effect prediction (Polyphen2, SIFT, PROVEAN), so it could be cited in Chapter 1's breast-cancer section or as methodological precedent for predicting functional consequences of missense variants in the MCF-7 WGS work in Chapter 5. It does not address ZFP36L1, replication stress or fragile sites.
446ca565d71b7fd7d1c84c2898f73cffcee17a2a: AURORA's multi-omics profiling of 381 paired primary/metastatic breast tumours is directly relevant to this thesis: it documents enrichment of driver mutations (ESR1, PTEN, PIK3CA, RB1) and clonality changes between primary and metastasis, and shows that high tumour mutational burden in HR+/HER2- disease predicts shorter relapse. Useful for Chapter 1's tumour-evolution and clonal-variations section (1.9) and the genome-wide WGS framing of Chapter 5. Provides a benchmark cohort against which the smaller MCF-7 WGS findings can be discussed.
25ef5dad03a7ff7f729dbd2f53ecb1fbb4582bde: General review of breast-cancer biomarkers covering nucleic-acid, protein and cellular markers, including circRNAs and miRNAs as diagnostic candidates. Useful as a broad citation for Chapter 1's breast-cancer overview (1.2) when motivating the search for genomic biomarkers, but the review does not engage with ZFP36L1, replication stress, fragile sites or the WGS mutational-burden framing that drives this thesis. Treat as background/context citation rather than mechanistic support.
aad85b7121b5d348fc49b8476ae3b502f528ce91: Foundational review reframing R loops from transcription byproducts to drivers of chromosome fragility and genome instability. Highly relevant to this thesis's replication-stress framing: ZFP36L1's role as an AU-rich-element RNA-binding protein places it close to the cotranscriptional R-loop literature, and predecessor work by Sidali (2023) in the same lab established R-loop accumulation at FRA14C in ZFP36L1-/- cells. Should be cited in Chapter 1's DNA-replication/replication-stress sections (1.12, 1.14) and revisited when interpreting genome-instability findings.
1459f37cf04e30db07f4c4b435a58fe9c4632941: Mechanistic study showing the Polϵ proofreading exonuclease and CTF18 cofactor act with PARP1 to prevent replication-fork collapse at single-ended DSBs caused by leading-strand encounters with single-strand breaks. Directly relevant to this thesis's replication-stress and DNA-damage-response themes (Chapter 1, sections 1.12-1.14): clarifies how forks fail and how fork-reversal pathways relate to HDR. Provides a current mechanistic citation that complements the older aphidicolin literature on stalled forks and licensing factors.
614259152d7fe4ee1f7c37530909bba354e2c24e: Review of DNA-damage-response defects in breast cancer and the resulting therapeutic vulnerabilities (platinum, PARP inhibitors, immunotherapy). Relevant to Chapter 1's section linking breast cancer to the DDR (1.8): supports the rationale that DDR pathway status shapes both carcinogenesis and treatment response. Less mechanistic than Aguilera 2012 or Ahmad 2023, but a useful clinically-oriented citation for situating the MCF-7 WGS work within the wider breast-cancer DDR landscape.
f6a781a0b4af0b3a313ea5fd6a19e38461dff0d1: Argues that positive selection on zinc-finger proteins in undifferentiated stem cells shaped mammalian adaptive evolution, suggesting these proteins acquired new transcriptional-regulation functions over time. Relevance to this thesis is thematic rather than mechanistic: ZFP36L1 is a zinc-finger RNA-binding protein, but this paper concerns evolutionary genetics of zinc-finger transcription factors rather than ZFP36L1 specifically or its replication-stress role. Could be cited in passing in Chapter 1's ZFP36L1 introduction (1.10) for the broader ZFP family context.
b85b1de4edc8954c3f670afe05c724086334db0a: Machine-learning analysis of prostate-cancer RNA-Seq identifying transcripts (HEATR5B, DDC, GABPB1-AS1) as candidate biomarkers. Marginally relevant to this thesis: the disease focus (prostate) and modality (transcriptomics, not WGS) sit outside the breast/osteosarcoma + WGS scope, and there is no engagement with ZFP36L1 or replication stress. Could be cited only as methodological precedent for NGS-derived biomarker discovery in Chapter 1's WGS-in-cancer section, but stronger options exist.
d022aefbea344df7e5912d9961e34da7997f640f: Review of S100 calcium-binding proteins in cancer, covering their roles in proliferation, apoptosis, inflammation and links to breast cancer, lung cancer and melanoma. Tangential to this thesis: S100 proteins are mechanistically unrelated to ZFP36L1 and were not identified as candidate hits in the MCF-7 or U2OS WGS top-mutated lists. Inclusion would only be warranted if a Chapter-5/6 candidate gene turns out to be an S100 family member; otherwise it can be omitted.
6cfe2d42afcf3e88fd62f3ef19a834445e70135c: Review of antitumour and proinflammatory immune responses in breast cancer, including immunotherapy strategies. Tangential to this thesis's genomic-instability focus, but provides broader breast-cancer biology context for Chapter 1's section 1.2 if the discussion touches on how genomic alterations interact with tumour-microenvironment immunity. No direct engagement with ZFP36L1 (which has well-documented immune-cell roles via mRNA decay) or with replication stress; could be cited if Chapter 1 broadens to immune-microenvironment context.
fcbb1b4c40158b198f471e88a2de59c6ae47a17e: Reviews the dual enhancer/promoter potential of regulatory DNA elements and the determinants of their transcriptional outputs. Relevance to this thesis is contingent: it becomes useful in Chapter 1's WGS sections (1.14, 1.15) when motivating interpretation of variants in non-coding regulatory regions, and in Chapter 5/6 if any candidate variants are found within enhancer or promoter elements. Not directly applicable to ZFP36L1 or replication-stress mechanism, but valuable for interpreting the non-coding mutational landscape.
02f3c4db03315c9379ab06d83c99abaebf24f161: Identifies CDT1, the DNA-replication licensing factor, as a candidate oncogene whose overexpression accelerates S-phase entry and is tumorigenic in NIH3T3 cells. Directly relevant to Chapter 1's section 1.12 on DNA replication and pre-replication-complex licensing: CDT1 dysregulation is a paradigmatic source of replication stress and re-replication, complementing cyclin-E and MCM-loading discussions already cited. Provides historical-mechanistic grounding for why licensing-factor imbalance matters in cancer and links cleanly to the aphidicolin/fork-stalling literature.
a905ea4fbe7fd74ea35f41da33b1f7c39fc721cd: Reviews how variation in non-coding regions and DNA methylation regulates HLA Class I/II gene expression, with implications for immune-related disease. Limited direct relevance to this thesis: HLA genes were not flagged in MCF-7 or U2OS top-mutated lists, and the thesis does not address tumour immunology. Could be cited in Chapter 1's WGS section if the discussion of non-coding-variant interpretation explicitly draws on HLA as an example, but stronger non-coding citations are likely available.
c4193bf31366b2f29b9a86e6d527e718a6d9c7cb: Reviews the MMTV-PyMT transgenic mouse as the most-used genetically engineered model of breast cancer, mapping its histological and molecular progression onto human disease. Useful for Chapter 1's animal-models-of-breast-cancer section (1.3) where mouse models are surveyed alongside other organisms. Does not engage with ZFP36L1 or replication stress, and the MCF-7/U2OS cellular models in this thesis are in vitro, but the citation supports broader rigour about how breast-cancer model systems compare.
291a485a9408d00a50a590679f816b542f25b20a: Recent review surveying precision-oncology methodologies — rapid sequencing, single-cell, spatial mapping, epigenetics, liquid biopsies — and their application to tumour heterogeneity, non-coding variation and inherited risk. Useful general citation for Chapter 1's WGS-in-cancer-research section (1.15) and Chapter 7's cross-lineage synthesis: it provides an up-to-date framing of how cancer genomics has matured beyond simple mutation calling. No direct ZFP36L1 or replication-stress engagement, but a strong methodological-context reference.
58678e273846d27976c636b917e27f03cb0d6076: Reviews physical and psychological functioning of older cancer survivors compared with non-cancer age-matched groups; concludes survivors fare worse on both dimensions but the literature is limited. Not relevant to this thesis's biological/genomic focus: there is no thematic overlap with ZFP36L1, replication stress, WGS or any cellular model used here. Recommend removal from the bibliography unless cited elsewhere in the thesis for a section the audit hasn't covered (e.g. a discussion of clinical implications in Chapter 8).
